How does Number One prevent AI sessions from losing context or repeating mistakes?

Long image

A

Answer

Number One attaches a hash-chained event stream to .numberone/ so every edit, crash, thought, and ruling replays across all 24+ AI harnesses without losing history.

  1. StreamStore writes every workspace fact to events.jsonl with canonical SHA-256 hashes and linear-time secret redaction.1
  2. ReplayEngine folds those atomic events into one verified WorkspaceProjection guarded by snapshotDigest.
  3. AuthorityEngine enforces L1 stream truth and L2 directives above L4 session prompts.2
  4. PartyModeOrchestrator runs three specialist officers and promotes new checks only when KPI delta exceeds zero.3

Applies toNumber One v1.0.0Node >= 22all MCP and CLI harnesses

1

How do workspace signals become authoritative state?

Diagram structure
  • Watchers & MCP sensors
  • Secret Redactor redact
  • events.jsonl log
  • ReplayEngine fold
  • Authority & Crew gate
  • Directory / GitHub / Jira mirrors
  • sensors → redact · raw events
  • redact → log · SHA-256
  • log → fold · JSONL
  • fold → gate · projection
  • log → mirrors · sync
  1. Watchers & MCP ↗

    Captures edits, Git hooks, test crashes, transcripts, and MCP calls.

  2. Secret Redactor ↗

    Scrubs cloud keys, PATs, JWTs, PEM blocks, and SAS tokens in linear time.

  3. events.jsonl ↗

    Links prevHash to hash and flushes bytes with fsyncSync.

  4. ReplayEngine ↗

    Rebuilds WorkspaceProjection and verifies snapshotDigest.

  5. Authority & Crew ↗

    Blocks L4 plans that violate L1 crashes, L2 directives, or L3 lessons.

How does L1–L4 arbitration stop repeated dead-ends?

Diagram structure
  • AI Harness agent
  • McpServer mcp
  • AuthorityEngine auth
  • StreamStore store
  • agent → mcp · consult_number_one
  • mcp → agent · lessons + dead-ends
  • agent → mcp · arbitrate_action
  • mcp → auth · check L1-L3 rules
  • auth → store · append arbitration.decided
  • store → mcp · seq + SHA-256 hash
  • mcp → agent · APPROVE or BLOCK
